title: Cerberus to Acquire Airbus US Space & Defense
html:
Cerberus Capital Management is acquiring the US space systems business of Airbus US Space & Defense, the investment firm announced Tuesday.

The acquisition is expected to close by the end of the year. The companies did not disclose the financial terms of the deal.

Cerberus’ POV: Under the deal, the firm will acquire the defense and space subsidiary’s 200,000 square foot product facility near Kennedy Space Center. Cerberus intends to invest in the “engineering organization, product portfolio, and US supply chain to build a leading independent, US-owned satellite platform,” according to a press release.

“With its strong flight track record, engineering depth, and production capability, the Business is well-positioned for growth as a trusted, independent merchant supplier of spacecraft,” Danil Subkhankulov, managing director of Cerberus Supply Chain, said in a statement. “We look forward to working alongside its talented team.”

Airbus’ POV: Airbus, the European parent company of the US subsidiary, is in the process of merging with other European space primes to create a joint venture that can compete with SpaceX’s Starlink. Under the merger, segments of Airbus, Leonardo, and Thales will partner as a new entity with a workforce of ~25,000 that’s expected to begin operations in 2027.
summary: Cerberus Capital Management is acquiring the US space systems business of Airbus US Space & Defense, the investment firm announced Tuesday.
